description: Enable config.json file watching in production mode so that settings, permissions, and plugin path changes are automatically detected and trigger rediscovery — without requiring a manual POST /reload or server restart. Currently, config watching is gated behind isDev(), meaning production users who edit config.json (e.g., adding a new instance URL) don't see their changes reflected until they manually reload. This change moves config watching out of the dev-only guard while keeping plugin file watchers (dist/ directory watchers) dev-only. Includes extensive E2E tests verifying production-mode config watching across multiple scenarios.

acceptanceCriteria: startConfigWatching is called in both isDev() and non-isDev() branches of reloadCore
startFileWatching and startPluginDirWatching remain gated behind isDev()

The reload.ts comment 'Production mode: static plugin discovery at startup; restart to reload' is updated to reflect config watching
The missed-config-write detection (prevConfigMtime comparison) also runs outside isDev()

userStories.title: Add production-mode server fixture to E2E tests
userStories.description: Add support for starting the MCP server in production mode (without --dev flag) in the E2E test fixtures, enabling tests that verify config watching works outside dev mode.
acceptanceCriteria: startMcpServer accepts a new option or parameter to start without --dev flag
When started without --dev, the server process does NOT receive --dev in its argv
When started without --dev, the server process does NOT have OPENTABS_DEV=1 in env
The existing tests that use startMcpServer(configDir, true) continue to work unchanged
userStories.notes:
Files:
- e2e/fixtures.ts (modify startMcpServer)

Context:
Currently `startMcpServer` has signature `(configDir, hot?, explicitPort?, envOverrides?)`. In non-hot mode (hot=false), it spawns `dist/index.js --dev`. There is no way to omit `--dev`.

Add a new optional parameter or options object. The simplest approach is to add a `prodMode?: boolean` parameter. When `prodMode` is true:
1. Spawn `dist/index.js` without `--dev` in nodeArgs
2. Do NOT set `OPENTABS_DEV` in the env

Current code (line 531-533):
```
    const nodeArgs = hot
      ? [path.join(SERVER_DIST_DIR, 'dev-proxy.js')]
      : [path.join(SERVER_DIST_DIR, 'index.js'), '--dev'];
```

After change:
```
    const nodeArgs = hot
      ? [path.join(SERVER_DIST_DIR, 'dev-proxy.js')]
      : prodMode
        ? [path.join(SERVER_DIST_DIR, 'index.js')]
        : [path.join(SERVER_DIST_DIR, 'index.js'), '--dev'];
```

And in the env object, conditionally exclude OPENTABS_DEV when prodMode is true (or just don't set it — it's not currently set anyway, since --dev comes from the CLI flag).

Also export the new option signature.

Constraints:
- Do NOT break existing callers — the parameter must be optional with a backward-compatible default.
- The `hot: true` mode (dev proxy) is not affected by this change.
- Keep the function signature clean — consider using an options object if adding a 5th positional param feels unwieldy. Check what existing callers look like.

userStories.title: E2E test: settings change derives new URL patterns in production mode
userStories.description: Write an E2E test verifying that adding url-type settings to config.json in production mode causes new URL patterns to be derived and reported in the health endpoint.
acceptanceCriteria: Test starts server in production mode with a plugin that has a url configSchema field
Test writes settings to config.json after startup
Health endpoint shows the derived URL pattern within 15 seconds without POST /reload
Multiple instances (e.g., prod + staging) both derive their own patterns
userStories.notes:
Files:
- e2e/config-watcher-prod.e2e.ts (append to existing file)

Context:
The e2e-test plugin already has configSchema with `instanceUrl` of type 'url'. See e2e/plugin-settings.e2e.ts line 69 for how the existing settings derivation test works (it uses POST /reload). This new test must NOT use POST /reload.

userStories.title: E2E test: permission change takes effect in production mode
userStories.description: Write an E2E test verifying that changing a plugin's permission in config.json in production mode is reflected in the server state without restart.
acceptanceCriteria: Test starts with a plugin at permission 'off'
Test updates config.json to set permission to 'auto'
Health endpoint or tool dispatch reflects the new permission without POST /reload
Server is in production mode
userStories.notes:
Files:
- e2e/config-watcher-prod.e2e.ts (append to existing file)

Context:
Permissions are stored in config.json under the `permissions` key. When config.json changes, the config watcher triggers reloadCore which re-reads permissions into state.pluginPermissions.

The test should:
1. Create temp config dir with e2e-test plugin, permission set to 'off' (not auto-approved)
2. Start server in production mode
3. Connect MCP client
4. Call a tool — verify it fails with permission error (or check health shows permission 'off')
5. Wait for config watcher log
6. Write config.json changing the permission to 'auto' with reviewedVersion matching plugin version
7. Poll until health endpoint shows the plugin with permission 'auto'
8. Verify tool call now succeeds (or health shows 'auto')

Check how permissions are structured in config: `{ permissions: { 'e2e-test': { permission: 'auto', reviewedVersion: '...' } } }`

The server version for the e2e-test plugin can be read from the plugin's package.json.

Constraints:
- Do NOT call POST /reload.
- Since OPENTABS_DANGEROUSLY_SKIP_PERMISSIONS=1 is set by the fixture, you may need to NOT set it for this specific test (override via envOverrides). Or instead of testing dispatch behavior, just verify the health endpoint reports the correct permission state.

userStories.title: E2E test: rapid config writes are debounced in production mode
userStories.description: Write an E2E test verifying that rapid successive writes to config.json are debounced into a single reload in production mode.
acceptanceCriteria: Test writes config.json 5+ times in rapid succession (< 50ms apart)
Only 1-2 reload log lines appear (not 5+), proving debounce works
Final state reflects the last written config
Server is in production mode
userStories.notes:
Files:
- e2e/config-watcher-prod.e2e.ts (append to existing file)

Context:
The config watcher uses a 200ms debounce timer (see file-watcher.ts line 637-647). Rapid writes within 200ms should only trigger one reload. The reload log line to look for is: 'Config watcher: config.json changed — triggering reload' (logged at line 642 of file-watcher.ts).

The test should:
1. Create temp config dir with empty localPlugins
2. Start server in production mode
3. Wait for config watcher to start
4. Write config.json 5 times rapidly (every 20ms) with different localPlugin paths (can use the same plugin path each time — the content change is what triggers the watcher)
5. Wait 2 seconds for all debounced reloads to complete
6. Count occurrences of 'config.json changed — triggering reload' in server logs
7. Assert count is <= 2 (debounce consolidated most writes)
8. Verify final state matches the last write (plugin tools present)

Constraints:
- The debounce interval is 200ms, so writes every 20ms should be well within the debounce window.
- Do NOT assert exactly 1 reload — timing can vary. Assert <= 2 is safe.
- Use server.logs (the captured stdout lines) to count occurrences.

userStories.title: E2E test: tools/list_changed notification sent to MCP clients after config change
userStories.description: Write an E2E test verifying that MCP clients receive a tools/list_changed notification after a config.json change adds or removes plugins in production mode.
acceptanceCriteria: Test connects an MCP client and listens for tools/list_changed notifications
After config.json is modified to add a plugin, client receives the notification
After receiving notification, client can list tools and see the new plugin's tools
Server is in production mode
userStories.notes:
Files:
- e2e/config-watcher-prod.e2e.ts (append to existing file)

Context:
When reloadCore completes, the caller (performConfigReload or the startup flow) calls notifyToolListChanged on all session servers. The MCP SDK emits this as a `notifications/tools/list_changed` JSON-RPC notification to connected clients.

The MCP client fixture (createMcpClient) likely has a way to subscribe to notifications or the client object may accumulate them. Check e2e/fixtures.ts for how McpClient is implemented — look for `onNotification` or a notifications array.

The test should:
1. Start server in production mode with empty localPlugins
2. Connect MCP client
3. Set up a notification listener (or check if the fixture has one)
4. Wait for config watcher log
5. Write config.json adding the e2e-test plugin
6. Wait for tools/list_changed notification (with timeout)
7. After receiving it, call listTools and verify new tools present

If the MCP client fixture doesn't expose notifications directly, check how other tests verify notifications — grep for 'list_changed' or 'notification' in e2e/*.ts files.

Constraints:
- This test verifies the notification mechanism, not just polling. If the client fixture doesn't support notification listening, the test should use a polling approach but assert that `tools/list_changed` appeared in some observable way.
